2609.14886.title: PeerPen: AI-Assisted Writing for Online Mental Health Peer Support
2609.14886.paper_summary: Online mental health communities thrive on peer support, yet those who volunteer to help often lack formal training and may struggle to articulate supportive responses. AI co-writing could lower this barrier; however, peer support derives much of its value from being perceived as personal, raising questions around authorship, ownership, and trust. We built PeerPen, a writing assistance tool embedded within a Reddit-like interface, supporting two main features: draft generation and revision of user-written responses. Through semi-structured interviews with 15 participants, we find that PeerPen reduced the burden of composing responses and increased confidence in offering support. Participants wanted AI to assist their writing without taking over authorship and anticipated tensions around authenticity and trust. Such assistance could make authorship uncertain even for responses written without it, weakening trust across the community. We contribute design implications for AI writing assistance that scaffolds supportive communication, preserves authorship, and accounts for community-level trust.
2609.14886.paper_summary_zh: 在線心理健康社群依賴於同儕支持，然而，志願提供幫助的人往往缺乏正式的訓練，並可能難以表達支持性的回應。AI 共同寫作可以降低這一障礙；然而，同儕支持的價值在於被視為個人化的，這引發了關於著作權、所有權和信任的問題。我們建造了 PeerPen，一個嵌入在類似 Reddit 界面的寫作輔助工具，支持兩個主要功能：草稿生成和用戶撰寫回應的修訂。通過對 15 位參與者進行半結構化訪談，我們發現 PeerPen 減輕了撰寫回應的負擔，並增加了提供支持的信心。參與者希望 AI 能夠協助他們的寫作，而不會接管著作權，並預期在真實性和信任方面會出現緊張。這種輔助甚至可能使未使用 AI 的回應的著作權變得不確定，削弱社群中的信任。我們為 AI 寫作輔助提供了設計啟示，以支撐支持性溝通，保留著作權，並考慮社群層級的信任。
